text: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is especially important in Cambodia's climate as the main medicine against heat stress. In broilers, mixed in drinking water: to boost immunity in day-old chicks in the first days (often with antibiotic), to reduce heat effects during the final week of growth when birds are panting (3 g per 10 kg of feed), and commonly for boars in the dry season to improve sperm quality (1 g per boar per day). Premixes are powdered vitamin/mineral products used mainly in pigs and poultry when farmers mix their own feed from local raw materials (commercial feed already includes them); premix composition differs by species and stage (e.g. sows need more vitamin A, D, E, and biotin than fattening pigs; layer and broiler premixes differ) — generic 'all species' premixes are often lower quality. Multivitamin powders provide higher vitamin levels than premixes and are mixed into pig feed mainly to help sick animals recover or support animals weakened by vaccination. For calcium/phosphorus specifically: layers need about 0.5 g of calcium daily for eggshell (oyster shell powder is a good source); other species need phosphorus alongside calcium for bone growth — DCP (a non-soluble white powder mixed into feed) works well, e.g. 10–20 g/day covers needs for growing pigs and lactating sows.
